He fought in the 1967 Six-Day War and was wounded. In 1968-69, he worked as a photographic model and began performing as a nightclub entertainer, quickly becoming well known throughout Israel.
family_context_summary: Geller was the son of Itzhaak Geller, a retired army sergeant major, and Margaret Freud. His parents divorced when he was 10, and his mother worked as a seamstress. He claims distant relation to Sigmund Freud on his mother's side.
parent_family_domain_summary: No clear evidence of family domain expertise in entertainment or performance. His father was a military sergeant major and his mother was a seamstress.
primary_early_advantage_tags: adversity,divorce,war service,direct audience exposure
evidence_summary: Geller grew up in modest circumstances with divorced parents and served as a paratrooper in the Six-Day War before beginning his entertainment career at age 22. He leveraged his charisma and controversial persona to build a national following in Israel through nightclub performances and media attention. No evidence of family wealth, domain expertise, or institutional pipelines was found in reviewed sources. His early success appears self-created through street-level performance and controversy-driven publicity.

name: Mukesh Ambani
milestone_by_age_26: At age 24 (1981), Ambani was given charge of constructing the Patalganga polyester filament yarn plant, a Rs 100 crore project, after his father Dhirubhai called him back from Stanford MBA studies to join Reliance Industries.
early_history_summary: Born in 1957 in Aden (Yemen) to Dhirubhai Ambani, founder of Reliance Industries, Mukesh moved to India as an infant. He grew up in a modest two-bedroom apartment in Mumbai. He earned a BE in chemical engineering from the Institute of Chemical Technology, then enrolled for an MBA at Stanford but withdrew in 1980 at his father's urging to help build Reliance, which was then a small but fast-growing enterprise. At age 24, he was handed responsibility for the Patalganga petrochemical plant construction.
family_context_summary: Born to Dhirubhai Ambani, founder of Reliance Industries, and Kokilaben Ambani. The family lived modestly in a two-bedroom apartment in Mumbai until the 1970s, though the father was building what would become India's largest company. Mukesh never received an allowance and used public transportation.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father Dhirubhai Ambani was the founder and builder of Reliance Industries, directly transferring business acumen, industry networks, and a corporate platform. Mukesh was called back from Stanford specifically to work in his father's company.
primary_early_advantage_tags: family business,father founder,corporate platform,chemical engineering,Stanford,networks
evidence_summary: Mukesh Ambani's early career was defined by his father Dhirubhai Ambani's existing business platform. He was pulled from Stanford to lead a major industrial project at age 24, leveraging his chemical engineering training and his father's corporate infrastructure, licenses, and networks. The family lived modestly early on, but Dhirubhai was already building Reliance into a major enterprise. Mukesh's success at Patalganga demonstrated execution capability within an inherited business platform rather than independent creation.

name: Iman
milestone_by_age_26: Discovered by American photographer Peter Beard in 1975 (age 20) while studying at the University of Nairobi; her first modeling assignment was for Vogue in 1976 (age 21), launching a career that made her one of the world's most iconic supermodels.
early_history_summary: Born Zara Mohamed Abdulmajid in Mogadiscio, Somalia, Iman was the daughter of a diplomat (Somali ambassador to Saudi Arabia) and a gynecologist. She was sent to boarding school in Egypt at age four and later moved to Kenya with her family. While studying political science at the University of Nairobi in 1975, she was discovered by photographer Peter Beard, who paid her tuition equivalent for a photo session. Beard took the photos to New York, and Iman was soon brought over, landing her first Vogue assignment in 1976.
family_context_summary: Iman's father was a diplomat serving as Somalia's ambassador to Saudi Arabia, and her mother was a gynecologist. She was the first girl in her paternal family in six generations of sons. She lived with grandparents during formative years and attended boarding school in Egypt from age four.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in fashion or modeling. Her father was a diplomat and her mother a physician, providing an educated, upper-middle-class background but no direct fashion industry connections.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Peter Beard discovery,diplomat family,boarding school,physical distinctiveness,Vogue
evidence_summary: Iman's modeling career was launched by chance discovery by photographer Peter Beard at age 20, which gave her immediate access to elite fashion networks and a Vogue assignment within a year. Her family background was professional (diplomat father, physician mother) but not fashion-connected. Her distinctive Somali features and long neck made her an instant success in the fashion world. The mentorship and promotion by Beard served as the primary catalyst for her early career.

name: Maurice Gibb
milestone_by_age_26: As a member of the Bee Gees, Maurice Gibb achieved international chart success with 'New York Mining Disaster 1941' (April 1967, age 17) and UK #1 'Massachusetts' (September 1967, age 17), following earlier Australian success with 'Spicks and Specks' (1966, age 16).
early_history_summary: Born in Douglas, Isle of Man, Maurice Gibb began his music career at age 5 in 1955, joining the skiffle group the Rattlesnakes with his brothers Barry and Robin. The family moved to Australia in 1958, where the Bee Gees formed. By 1966, the group had an Australian #1 hit with 'Spicks and Specks.' They returned to England in early 1967, signed with Robert Stigwood, and quickly achieved international chart success with 'New York Mining Disaster 1941' and 'Massachusetts' that same year. Maurice served as bassist, guitarist, and vocalist for the group.
family_context_summary: Maurice was the son of Hugh Gibb, a drummer, and Barbara Gibb. He was born 35 minutes after his fraternal twin Robin, with older brother Barry. The family was deeply musical, with Hugh Gibb's drumming background and the brothers harmonizing from a young age. The family moved from the Isle of Man to Manchester, then to Australia in 1958 to support the boys' musical career.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father Hugh Gibb was a drummer, providing direct musical domain exposure. The parents actively supported and managed the brothers' musical development, relocating from the Isle of Man to Manchester and then to Australia to advance their career opportunities.
primary_early_advantage_tags: sibling band,twin brother,father drummer,early performance,Australia,Stigwood,harmonizing
evidence_summary: Maurice Gibb's career was defined by the sibling collaboration with brothers Barry and Robin from age 5, creating one of the most successful pop groups in history. His father Hugh was a drummer, providing early musical exposure, and the family relocated internationally to support the boys' career. The brothers accumulated thousands of hours of performance and harmonizing practice before their international breakthrough at ages 16-17. The high-trust sibling team, combined with early performance experience and manager Robert Stigwood's network, created a uniquely powerful launch platform.

name: Akinori Nakayama
milestone_by_age_26: Won six medals including three gold at the 1966 World Championships in Dortmund (age 23), then became the most successful male athlete at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics with four gold, one silver, and one bronze (age 25).
early_history_summary: Born in Nagoya, Japan, Nakayama was a graduate of Chukyo University in Nagoya. He won the all-around at the 1965 and 1967 Universiade competitions. His first major international breakthrough came at the 1966 World Championships in Dortmund, where he won six medals including three gold (team, floor exercise, horizontal bar). He followed this with four gold medals at the 1968 Olympics, becoming the most successful male athlete of those Games.
family_context_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. Nakayama was born in Nagoya and graduated from Chukyo University, but family background details were not found.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Chukyo University,Japanese gymnastics system,1965 Universiade,world champion,Olympic champion
evidence_summary: Nakayama was a product of the dominant Japanese men's gymnastics pipeline of the 1960s, graduating from Chukyo University in Nagoya, a city with strong gymnastics traditions. He won the Universiade all-around in 1965 (age 22) and 1967, demonstrating early competitive success before his World Championship breakthrough at 23. The Japanese gymnastics system provided elite coaching, training facilities, and a competitive team environment. Family background details were not documented in reviewed sources, so early-advantage scores are conservative.

name: István Sándorfi
milestone_by_age_26: Had his first individual exhibition at a small gallery in Paris at age 17 (1965), followed by a second exhibition in 1966, and his first significant museum exhibition at the Musée d'Art Moderne de la Ville de Paris in 1973 (age 25).
early_history_summary: Born in Budapest in 1948, Sándorfi's father was director of IBM in Hungary, which led to the father's imprisonment under the Communist regime and the family's deportation to a village. During the 1956 Hungarian uprising, the family fled to Germany and then France. Deeply affected by the violence of the revolution, István took refuge in drawing and then oil painting at age 12. Art became his overriding passion, and at age 17, while still in secondary school, he had his first solo exhibition in Paris. He later attended the École des Beaux-Arts and École des Arts Décoratifs.
family_context_summary: Sándorfi's father was director of IBM in Hungary, indicating an upper-middle-class professional background. The father was imprisoned for five years under Communist rule due to his IBM association, and the family was deported to an isolated village before fleeing Hungary in 1956. The family eventually settled in France.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in visual arts. His father was a corporate executive (IBM director), not an artist. However, the family's professional status may have facilitated access to education and galleries in Paris after emigration.
primary_early_advantage_tags: 1956 refugee,father imprisoned,self-taught painting,Paris galleries,obsessive practice,oil painting age 12
evidence_summary: Sándorfi's early career was shaped by the trauma of his father's imprisonment and the family's flight from Hungary in 1956. He channeled this into an obsessive dedication to drawing and painting from age 12, producing work mature enough for a solo gallery exhibition by age 17. His father's professional background (IBM director) provided some cultural capital but no direct art-world connections. The displacement to Paris placed him in a major art capital, and his self-driven, visceral approach to painting set him apart. His father later enrolled him at the École des Beaux-Arts to give him a more prestigious status.

name: Oliviero Toscani
milestone_by_age_26: After graduating from the Kunstgewerbeschule Zürich in 1965 (age 23), Toscani published his first fashion story in Annabelle magazine, leading to work with Harper's Bazaar and his first Vogue Italia shoot in 1967 (age 25), establishing him with major international fashion magazines by his mid-20s.
early_history_summary: Born in Milan in 1942, Toscani grew up in his father Fedele Toscani's photographic world. His father was a famous photojournalist for Corriere della Sera, and Toscani acted as his lab assistant and messenger from childhood. He had his first published photo at age 14. He studied photography and graphic design at the Kunstgewerbeschule Zürich from 1961 to 1965, learning from teachers who came directly from the Bauhaus. After graduating, his first reportage story of a girl in a miniskirt was published by Annabelle magazine, which led to fashion photography work for Harper's Bazaar, French Elle, and Italian and British Vogue.
family_context_summary: Toscani was born into a photography family. His father Fedele Toscani was a renowned photojournalist for Corriere della Sera, famous for photographing the hanging corpses of Mussolini. Toscani acted as his father's lab assistant and messenger from a young age, giving him early immersion in the world of photojournalism. He had his first published photo at age 14.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father Fedele Toscani was a prominent Italian photojournalist who founded the Publifoto and Rotofoto photographic agencies and worked for Corriere della Sera. This provided direct domain expertise, darkroom access, press contacts, and an early understanding of the power of images.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father photojournalist,darkroom access,Corriere della Sera,Kunstgewerbeschule Zurich,Bauhaus teachers,Vogue Italia,fashion photography
evidence_summary: Toscani's early career was built on a deep family-domain apprenticeship: his father was a famous photojournalist who provided darkroom access, press world exposure, and an early understanding of visual storytelling from childhood. This was complemented by formal training at the Kunstgewerbeschule Zürich under Bauhaus-trained teachers. By his early 20s, he was working for major international fashion magazines including Vogue Italia, Harper's Bazaar, and French Elle. His father's profession gave him both technical skills and industry fluency that most young photographers would lack.

name: Ronaldo
milestone_by_age_26: Named 1996 FIFA World Player of the Year at age 20 (youngest recipient ever); won 1997 Ballon d'Or at 21 (also youngest ever); won 2002 FIFA World Cup at 25 scoring twice in the final.
early_history_summary: Born in Itaguí, Rio de Janeiro, Ronaldo grew up in a poor family and started playing futsal at age 12, scoring a record 166 goals in his first season. Spotted by former Brazil star Jairzinho, he joined São Cristóvão's youth team and was recommended to Cruzeiro at 16. He scored 56 goals in 58 games for Cruzeiro before moving to PSV Eindhoven in 1994, then Barcelona in 1996 for a world-record transfer fee.
family_context_summary: Ronaldo was born to Sônia dos Santos Barata and Nélio Nazário de Lima. His parents separated when he was 11. The family was poor — his mother borrowed money from relatives for bus fare to take him to a Flamengo trial. He grew up on the streets of Rio with a ball at his feet.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in football. His father worked various jobs and the family struggled financially.
primary_early_advantage_tags: brazilian-football-pipeline, prodigy-physical-talent, futsal-development, jairzinho-discovery, cruzeiro-to-european-clubs
evidence_summary: Ronaldo's extraordinary physical talent — pace, power, dribbling, and finishing — was evident from his futsal days in Rio. The Brazilian football pipeline, from São Cristóvão to Cruzeiro to PSV to Barcelona, provided a structured elite pathway that accelerated his development. Jairzinho's discovery of him at São Cristóvão was a key mentor connection. His poverty and family separation created urgency but also meant no financial safety net. By 20, he was FIFA World Player of the Year; by 21, Ballon d'Or winner — both youngest ever.

name: Pat Patterson
milestone_by_age_26: Won the NWA Pacific Northwest Heavyweight Championship in October 1964 at age 23, and the NWA World Tag Team Championship with Ray Stevens in 1965 at age 24 as part of the Blond Bombers.
early_history_summary: Born Pierre Clermont in Montreal in 1941, Patterson grew up in poverty as one of nine siblings in a two-bedroom apartment. He was introduced to wrestling at 14, training with Gilles 'Cyclone' Samson, and debuted professionally in 1958 at age 17. He moved to Boston in 1961, then to Pacific Northwest Wrestling in 1962, where he developed the 'Pretty Boy' character and won regional championships by 1964.
family_context_summary: Patterson was the son of a milkman and grew up in extreme poverty in Montreal, one of nine siblings in a two-bedroom apartment with no hot water. He came out as gay at 16 and was rejected by his father, who told him to leave home. He immigrated to the US in 1961 despite speaking no English.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in wrestling or entertainment. His father was a milkman and the family lived in poverty.
primary_early_advantage_tags: poverty, gay-rejection, early-wrestling-training, tag-team-with-ray-stevens, regional-wrestling-territories
evidence_summary: Patterson's path was defined by extreme adversity — poverty, a father who rejected him for being gay, and immigration to a foreign country at 20 with no English. He started wrestling training at 14 and debuted at 17, accumulating years of reps before his first championship at 23. His tag team partnership with Ray Stevens, described by Bret Hart as possibly the best tag team of the 1970s, was a critical complementary relationship. The regional wrestling territory system of the 1960s provided the ecosystem in which he could build a career.

name: Garry Kasparov
milestone_by_age_26: Became the youngest undisputed World Chess Champion in history in November 1985 at age 22 by defeating Anatoly Karpov, a record that stood until 2024.
early_history_summary: Born Garik Weinstein in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR, Kasparov began studying chess at age 7 after solving a chess problem his parents had set up. At 10, he entered Mikhail Botvinnik's chess school under coach Vladimir Makogonov. He won the Soviet Junior Championship at 13, the Banja Luka tournament at 16, the World Junior Championship at 17, and became a Grandmaster in 1980 at 17. He became world No. 1 in January 1984 at age 21 and world champion in 1985 at 22.
family_context_summary: Kasparov's father, Kim Moiseyevich Weinstein, was Jewish and died of leukemia when Kasparov was 7. His mother, Klara Shagenovna Kasparova, was Armenian. At 12, he adopted his mother's surname. The family fled anti-Armenian pogroms in Baku in January 1990.
parent_family_domain_summary: His parents set up chess problems that sparked his interest, and his father admired intellectual figures. However, no evidence of professional chess background in the family. His father's early death meant his mother raised him and guided his chess career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: botvinnik-chess-school, soviet-chess-pipeline, child-prodigy, makogonov-coaching, young-pioneer-palace
evidence_summary: Kasparov's trajectory was shaped by the Soviet chess pipeline and elite mentoring. From age 10, he trained at Botvinnik's chess school under Makogonov, who developed his positional skills. Botvinnik declared at 11 that 'the future of chess lies in the hands of this young man.' His prodigy-level ability was evident early — Soviet Junior Champion at 13, Grandmaster at 17, world No. 1 at 21. The Soviet state provided the institutional infrastructure, while Botvinnik's school offered sustained, high-level coaching. His father's death at 7 and later fleeing pogroms created adversity but also focus.
starting_point: Born in 1963 in Baku, Azerbaijan SSR, Soviet Union, to a Jewish father and Armenian mother; father died when he was seven, and he took his mother's surname Kasparova.
current_position: Former World Chess Champion living in exile from Russia; chairman of the Human Rights Foundation; author and pro-democracy activist opposing Vladimir Putin.

name: Sawao Kato
milestone_by_age_26: Won three gold medals (team, all-around, floor exercise) and a bronze (rings) at the 1968 Mexico City Olympics at age 22; won four more medals including two golds at the 1972 Munich Olympics at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Niigata Prefecture, Japan, Kato originally wanted to play baseball but was steered toward gymnastics by a PE teacher in junior high school. He became a 'secret gymnast' who practiced without telling his parents. He studied at Tokyo Kyoiku University (now University of Tsukuba) under coach Akitomo Kaneko, and made the Japanese national team at 18. At 22, he won three Olympic gold medals in Mexico City.
family_context_summary: Kato was one of five children, born in Niigata Prefecture. His father was a railway engineer. He shone academically as a child and showed little early interest in sport before being discovered by a PE teacher. His elder brother Takeshi also competed in gymnastics at the Olympics.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in gymnastics. His father was a railway engineer. His elder brother Takeshi was also an Olympic gymnast, suggesting sibling influence rather than parental transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: japanese-gymnastics-dominance, tokyo-kyoiku-university, coach-kaneko, olympic-team, sibling-gymnast
evidence_summary: Kato benefited from Japan's dominance in men's gymnastics during the 1960s-70s, the strongest national program in the sport. The pipeline from junior high discovery to Tokyo Kyoiku University under coach Akitomo Kaneko to the national team was a structured elite pathway. His elder brother Takeshi provided a sibling peer in gymnastics. Kato was renowned for self-discipline and innovative training methods, including using the trampoline to practice routines. His PE teacher's early identification of his potential was a key mentor moment, though not a sustained individualized relationship.

name: Klaus Schulze
milestone_by_age_26: Released debut solo album 'Irrlicht' in 1972 at age 25, after being a founding member of Tangerine Dream (1969) and co-founding Ash Ra Tempel (1970), two of the most influential Krautrock bands.
early_history_summary: Born in Berlin in 1947, Schulze's father was a writer and his mother a ballet dancer. He played guitar, bass, and drums in local bands during the 1960s, including a band called Psy Free. In 1969, he became the drummer for Tangerine Dream on their debut album 'Electronic Meditation.' He left in 1970 to co-found Ash Ra Tempel with Manuel Göttsching, then left after one album to launch a solo career with 'Irrlicht' in 1972.
family_context_summary: Schulze was born in Berlin in 1947. His father was a writer and his mother a ballet dancer, providing an arts-oriented family background. He studied German at Technische Universität Berlin after graduating from high school.
parent_family_domain_summary: His father was a writer and his mother a ballet dancer, suggesting an arts-oriented household that may have fostered creative sensibilities, though no direct music domain transfer is documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: west-berlin-krautrock-scene, tangerine-dream, ash-ra-tempel, manuel-gottsching, edgar-froese, zodiac-club
evidence_summary: Schulze was immersed in the West Berlin experimental music scene of the late 1960s, a frontier of electronic and psychedelic music. His parents' artistic backgrounds (writer father, ballet dancer mother) provided a creative household. The key accelerant was his peer network — Edgar Froese of Tangerine Dream, Manuel Göttsching of Ash Ra Tempel — collaborators who collectively defined the Krautrock and Berlin School electronic music movements. His rapid progression from drummer to solo electronic artist in just three years (1969-1972) reflects both the ferment of the scene and his own distinctive creative vision.

name: Vassily Ivanchuk
milestone_by_age_26: Won the 1988 New York Open at age 19 (ahead of a field of grandmasters), was awarded the Grandmaster title in 1988, tied for first at the World Junior Chess Championship, and won the elite Linares super-tournament in 1989 at age 20.
early_history_summary: Born in Kopychyntsi, Ukrainian SSR, Ivanchuk began playing chess after his father bought him a magnetic chess set for his birthday. His father was a lawyer and his mother a physics teacher. He won the USSR Junior Chess Championship in 1985 at age 16, the European Junior Chess Championship in 1986/87, and achieved international notice by winning the 1988 New York Open. He became a Grandmaster in 1988 and won Linares in 1989.
family_context_summary: Ivanchuk's father was a lawyer and his mother was a physics teacher, providing an educated household. His father bought him a magnetic chess set that sparked his interest in the game. No evidence of significant financial advantage or hardship.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in chess. His father was a lawyer and mother a physics teacher — an educated family but not a chess-specific domain advantage.
primary_early_advantage_tags: soviet-chess-pipeline, ussr-junior-championship, ukrainian-chess, educated-family, early-grandmaster
evidence_summary: Ivanchuk's rise was facilitated by the Soviet chess pipeline, which identified and developed talent through systematic competition structures. Winning the USSR Junior Championship at 16 and the European Junior Championship at 17/18 provided the credentials for international competition. His educated family background (lawyer father, physics teacher mother) may have supported intellectual development. No specific sustained mentor is documented. His Grandmaster title at 19 and New York Open victory the same year marked him as an elite player. The Soviet chess system was the dominant institutional ecosystem.

name: Fernando Alonso
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Formula One World Drivers' Championship in 2005 at age 24 (then youngest ever) with Renault, and successfully defended the title in 2006 at age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Oviedo, Spain to a working-class family, Alonso began karting at age 7. He won the CIK-FIA Five Continents Cup in 1996 at age 15, progressed to junior formulae at 17, winning the Euro Open by Nissan in 1999 and finishing fourth in International Formula 3000 in 2000. He signed for Minardi in 2001, making his F1 debut at 20, then joined Renault as a test driver before becoming a race driver and winning the world championship in 2005.
family_context_summary: Alonso was born and raised in Oviedo, Asturias, Spain, to a working-class family. His father was a mechanic in an explosives factory and his mother worked in a department store. The family made significant financial sacrifices to support his karting career from age 7.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in motorsport. His father was a mechanic, which may have provided some mechanical aptitude, but not racing-specific domain knowledge.
primary_early_advantage_tags: karting-from-age-7, euro-open-by-nissan, f1-pipeline, renault-team, working-class-sacrifices, adrian-campos
evidence_summary: Alonso's career was built on extreme early specialization — karting from age 7 with family sacrifices, progressing through a structured European junior formulae pipeline (Euro Open by Nissan, F3000) to F1. The karting-to-F1 pipeline is one of the most selective performance pathways in sport. His working-class background meant no financial safety net; the family's sacrifices and his talent combined to create urgency. The Renault team provided the complementary team structure for his championship wins. By 24, he was the youngest F1 world champion in history at the time.
starting_point: Born in Oviedo, Asturias, Spain to a working-class family; father was a mechanic in an explosives factory and mother worked in a department store; family made significant financial sacrifices to support his karting from age 7.
current_position: Racing for Aston Martin in Formula One; estimated net worth ~$240 million; first driver to reach 400 Grand Prix starts; contracted through 2026.

name: Jeff Beck
milestone_by_age_26: Joined the Yardbirds in March 1965 at age 21 as Eric Clapton's replacement; formed the Jeff Beck Group in 1967 with Rod Stewart and Ronnie Wood; released two albums ('Truth' in 1968, 'Beck-Ola' in 1969) by age 25.
early_history_summary: Born Geoffrey Arnold Beck in Wallington, Surrey, he became interested in the electric guitar as a child after hearing Les Paul. He sang in a church choir at 10, learned guitar as a teenager on a borrowed instrument, and attended Wimbledon School of Art. His sister Annetta introduced him to Jimmy Page. He played in several bands in the early 1960s before joining the Yardbirds in March 1965, where he recorded most of their Top 40 hits including the album 'Roger the Engineer' (1966).
family_context_summary: Beck was born to Arnold and Ethel Beck at 206 Demesne Road, Wallington, Surrey. He had a sister, Annetta, who introduced him to Jimmy Page. He attended Wimbledon School of Art (now Wimbledon College of Arts). No evidence of significant family wealth or hardship.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in music. His sister Annetta's connection to Jimmy Page was a meaningful network introduction, but not a family domain transfer.
primary_early_advantage_tags: london-1960s-rock-scene, yardbirds, jimmy-page-via-sister, rod-stewart, ronnie-wood, british-blues-explosion
evidence_summary: Beck was immersed in the London/Surrey rock and blues scene of the 1960s, the global frontier of rock guitar innovation. His sister's introduction to Jimmy Page provided a critical peer network connection. The Yardbirds, already an established band when he joined as Clapton's replacement, gave him a platform. His complementary team with Rod Stewart and Ronnie Wood in the Jeff Beck Group produced two influential albums by age 25. His distinctive guitar technique — described as a 'guitarist's guitarist' — was a rare skill that set him apart even in the competitive 1960s London scene.

name: Dikembe Mutombo
milestone_by_age_26: Selected 4th overall in the 1991 NBA draft at age 25 and named to the NBA All-Rookie First Team in 1992; was a 2x Big East Defensive Player of the Year and All-American at Georgetown by age 25.
early_history_summary: Born in Kinshasa, DRC, Mutombo was the son of a school principal and one of 10 siblings. He attended Boboto College in Kinshasa and came to the US at age 21 on a USAID scholarship to attend Georgetown University, originally intending to study medicine. Georgetown basketball coach John Thompson recruited him to play basketball. He played three seasons (1988-1991), becoming 2x Big East Defensive Player of the Year and an All-American, before being drafted 4th overall by the Denver Nuggets in 1991.
family_context_summary: Mutombo was born to Samuel and Biamba Marie Mutombo in Kinshasa. His father was a school principal. He had 9 siblings. The family was educated but not wealthy. His father and brother encouraged him to take up basketball due to his height.
parent_family_domain_summary: No evidence of family domain expertise in basketball. His father was a school principal, providing an education-oriented household. The family's encouragement to pursue basketball was based on his physical stature rather than domain knowledge.
primary_early_advantage_tags: georgetown-university, john-thompson-coaching, 7ft-2-height, usaid-scholarship, alonzo-mourning-teammate, nba-draft-4th-overall
evidence_summary: Mutombo's path was defined by his extraordinary physical advantage (7'2" height) combined with the Georgetown University basketball pipeline under coach John Thompson, who provided sustained, high-quality coaching that developed him from a raw athlete into an All-American and top-5 NBA draft pick. The USAID scholarship that brought him from Congo to Georgetown was a critical institutional bridge. His teammate Alonzo Mourning provided a high-level peer environment. He started basketball late (~age 16) but his physical edge and Thompson's coaching accelerated his development rapidly. The cultural adjustment from Congo to US college basketball was a formative adversity.

name: Richard Stallman
milestone_by_age_26: Developed Emacs, the first extensible customizable self-documenting display editor, at the MIT AI Lab in 1976 (age 23), and published the EMACS paper as MIT AI Memo 519 in June 1979 (age 26).
early_history_summary: Stallman was programming from high school, hired at the IBM New York Scientific Center in summer 1970, and became a programmer at the MIT Artificial Intelligence Laboratory in 1971 during his first year at Harvard. He quickly became a central figure in the MIT hacker community, developing system software including Emacs (1976) and the AI technique of dependency-directed backtracking (1975), all before age 26.
family_context_summary: Born in Manhattan in 1953 to a family of Jewish heritage. He had a troublesome relationship with his parents and did not feel he had a proper home, finding a sense of belonging only at Harvard and the MIT AI Lab.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental computing or technical expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIT AI Lab, Harvard, PDP-10, ITS, hacker community, time-sharing systems
evidence_summary: Stallman gained access to the MIT AI Lab — the premier computing research environment of the era — during his first year at Harvard in 1971, and became a central figure in its hacker community. He had rare early access to PDP-10 computers and the ITS time-sharing system, which were extremely scarce for the era. His sustained immersion in this elite ecosystem enabled him to develop Emacs by age 23. Family background provided no domain advantage; his drive was self-created, partly catalyzed by feeling like an outsider in his family life. name: John Walker

name: Kate Bush
milestone_by_age_26: Topped the UK singles chart for four weeks in March 1978 at age 19 with her debut single 'Wuthering Heights,' becoming the first female artist to achieve a UK number one with a fully self-written song; her debut album The Kick Inside sold over a million copies.

name: George Weah
milestone_by_age_26: Signed for AS Monaco in 1988 at age 22 after being discovered by Arsène Wenger, was named African Footballer of the Year in 1989 at age 23, won the Coupe de France with Monaco in 1991, and helped Monaco reach the European Cup Winners' Cup final in 1992 before signing for PSG at age 26.

name: Gheorghe Hagi
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Divizia A (Romanian top division) debut at age 17 in 1982-83 for FC Constanța, then scored 58 goals in 108 appearances for Sportul Studențesc between 1983 and 1986 (ages 18-21), becoming one of Romania's most prodigious young talents and drawing the attention of dictator Ceaușescu before transferring to Steaua București in 1986.

name: Jimmy Page
milestone_by_age_26: Played on the UK No. 1 single 'Diamonds' by Jet Harris and Tony Meehan in early 1963 at age 19, becoming one of London's most sought-after session guitarists by the mid-1960s. He joined the Yardbirds in 1966 at age 22 and founded Led Zeppelin in 1968 at age 24.

name: Jean-Claude Van Damme
milestone_by_age_26: Won the European Karate Championship as a member of the Belgian Karate Team on 26 December 1979 at age 19, and won the Mr. Belgium bodybuilding title in 1978 at age 17-18. name: John Lydon
milestone_by_age_26: Became lead vocalist of the Sex Pistols in 1975 at age 19. name: Zlatan Ibrahimović
milestone_by_age_26: Joined Ajax in July 2001 at age 19-20 and won the 2001-02 Eredivisie title. name: Roger Waters
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Pink Floyd in 1965 at age 22 and released the debut album 'The Piper at the Gates of Dawn' on 4 August 1967 at age 23, which reached number 6 on the UK charts. milestone_by_age_26: Made Formula One debut with Sauber in 2001 at age 21, achieved maiden podium on debut with McLaren in 2002, won first Grand Prix at Malaysia in 2003 at age 23, and won seven Grands Prix finishing runner-up to Fernando Alonso in the 2005 championship at age 26.

His first solo album came at 19 and the national flamenco competition win at 20.

parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a flamenco guitarist who received guitar lessons himself and introduced Paco to the guitar at age 5. name: Brian Jones
milestone_by_age_26: Founded the Rolling Stones in 1962 at age 20, gave the band its name, and played their first gig at the Marquee Club on 12 July 1962. He left home for London, became a blues musician calling himself 'Elmo Lewis,' and placed an ad in Jazz News in May 1962 auditioning musicians for a new R&B group. He founded the Rolling Stones, named the band, and was its initial leader and musical force before Jagger and Richards emerged as songwriters.
family_context_summary: Middle-class parents in Cheltenham. Father Lewis Blount Jones was an aeronautical engineer and piano teacher. name: Bobby Moore
milestone_by_age_26: Made his West Ham United first-team debut on 8 September 1958 at age 17, earned his first England cap on 20 May 1962 at age 21, played in the 1962 World Cup, and became the youngest man ever to captain England on 29 May 1963 at age 22 — all well before age 26.

He made his England debut against Peru in May 1962 and captained England for the first time in May 1963 at age 22, the youngest ever at the time. He went on to captain England to World Cup victory in 1966 at age 25.

He earned his England cap at 21, played in the 1962 World Cup, and became England's youngest-ever captain at 22. He later captained England to World Cup victory in 1966 at age 25.

name: Bobby Fischer

By age 26 he had won eight U.S. Championships and was a World Championship candidate.

name: Luka Modrić
milestone_by_age_26: Won six domestic trophies with Dinamo Zagreb, was named Player of the Year in the Bosnian league on loan at age 18, and earned a £16.5m transfer to Tottenham Hotspur in 2008 at age 23, becoming a Croatia international since 2006.
early_history_summary: Born in Zadar, Croatia (then Yugoslavia), Modrić grew up in the hamlet of Modrići on the slopes of Velebit mountain. His grandfather was killed by Serbian forces in December 1991, and his family became refugees living in hotels in Zadar during the Croatian War of Independence. He played football on hotel parking lots, joined NK Zadar's academy, and was signed by Dinamo Zagreb at age 16. He was loaned to Zrinjski Mostar in Bosnia at 18, where he won Player of the Year.
family_context_summary: Modrić grew up as a war refugee; his grandfather was killed by Serbian military forces in December 1991. The family lived in dilapidated hotels in Zadar as refugees. His father's occupation is not clearly documented in reviewed sources.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No family football connections found.
primary_early_advantage_tags: war refugee, grandfather killed, football as escape, early academy entry, loan spell in Bosnia, mentor coach
evidence_summary: Modrić's early career was shaped by the Croatian War of Independence, which killed his grandfather and made his family refugees. Football became his escape, playing on hotel parking lots before joining NK Zadar and then Dinamo Zagreb at 16. He was rejected by Hajduk Split for being too small and weak, but persevered through punishing loan spells in Bosnia. Coach Tomislav Basic at NK Zadar was his 'sporting father' who facilitated his move to Dinamo Zagreb. By 23, he had won six domestic trophies and earned a record £16.5m transfer to Tottenham.

name: Fabio Cannavaro
milestone_by_age_26: Made his Serie A debut for Napoli in 1993 at age 19, then won the UEFA Cup and Coppa Italia with Parma by 1999 (age 25-26), and became an Italy international in 1997, all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Naples to a bank clerk father and a maid mother, Cannavaro grew up in the Rione La Loggetta neighborhood. He was a ball boy at Napoli's Stadio San Paolo at age 13 when the club won its first Serie A title in 1987. He joined Napoli's youth academy, trained alongside Maradona and Ciro Ferrara, and made his first-team debut in 1993 under coach Claudio Ranieri. He moved to Parma in 1995, where he won the UEFA Cup and two Coppa Italia titles.
family_context_summary: Father was a bank clerk who also played football for provincial side Giugliano. Mother worked as a maid. Younger brother Paolo also became a professional footballer. Working-class family in Naples.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father played football at a provincial level and younger brother Paolo became a professional footballer, suggesting a family football culture, though not at elite level.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Napoli youth academy, Maradona era immersion, ball boy to player, father played football, brother professional, working-class Naples, Serie A debut at 19
evidence_summary: Cannavaro's path was defined by immersion in Napoli's youth system during the Maradona era, where he was a ball boy at 13 and trained with the first team alongside Maradona and Ciro Ferrara. His father played football at provincial level and his brother Paolo also became professional, indicating a family football culture. Despite being 5'9" and from a working-class family, he debuted in Serie A at 19 and won the UEFA Cup with Parma by 25. The Napoli youth academy and proximity to elite players like Maradona provided a rare developmental environment.

name: John Bonham
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Led Zeppelin in 1968 at age 20 and played on their debut album released in January 1969, launching one of the most successful rock bands in history well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Redditch, Worcestershire, Bonham began drumming at age 5 using household containers and coffee tins. His mother bought him a snare drum at 10 and his parents bought him a full drum kit at 15. He never took formal lessons. He played in multiple local bands from the early 1960s, including Terry Webb and The Spiders, The Senators, and Way Of Life, building a reputation as one of the best drummers in the Midlands. In 1968, he joined Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, and John Paul Jones to form Led Zeppelin.
family_context_summary: Father Jack was a carpenter who ran the family building business (JH Bonham & Son). Mother Joan ran a local newsagent's shop. The dual family incomes enabled Bonham to attend Wilton House private school. Parents supported his drumming, buying him a snare drum at 10 and a full kit at 15.
parent_family_domain_summary: No family music background documented. Father was a carpenter/builder, mother ran a newsagent's shop.
primary_early_advantage_tags: drumming from age 5, no formal lessons, parents bought drum kit, Midlands music scene, relentless gigging, Led Zeppelin team, hard rock wave
evidence_summary: Bonham was a natural drumming prodigy who started at age 5 without formal lessons and built his skills through relentless gigging in Midlands bands from his mid-teens. His parents, a carpenter father and newsagent mother, supported his passion by buying him drums. By his early twenties, he had a reputation as one of the most powerful drummers in the region. Joining Jimmy Page, Robert Plant, and John Paul Jones in 1968 to form Led Zeppelin created one of rock's greatest complementary teams, riding the hard rock wave to immediate success with their 1969 debut album.

name: John Travolta
milestone_by_age_26: Became a teen idol starring as Vinnie Barbarino in Welcome Back, Kotter (1975) at age 21, then achieved international stardom with Saturday Night Fever (1977) at age 23, earning an Academy Award nomination for Best Actor.
early_history_summary: Born in Englewood, New Jersey, Travolta was the youngest of six children in a family of entertainers. His mother Helen was an actress, singer, and high school drama teacher who inspired all six children to pursue acting. His father Salvatore was a semiprofessional football player turned tire salesman. With his parents' approval, Travolta dropped out of high school at 16 to pursue acting, landing off-Broadway roles (Rain, 1972), Broadway roles (Grease touring company, Over Here! 1974), and his star-making TV role in Welcome Back, Kotter (1975).
family_context_summary: Mother Helen Cecilia (née Burke) was an actress, singer, and high school drama and English teacher who had appeared in radio vocal group The Sunshine Sisters. Father Salvatore was a semiprofessional football player turned tire salesman and partner in Travolta Tire Exchange. All five siblings (Joey, Ellen, Ann, Margaret, Sam) became actors. Irish-Italian American Catholic family.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was an actress and drama teacher who directly trained and inspired all six children to become actors. This is a clear case of family-domain apprenticeship in performing arts.
primary_early_advantage_tags: mother drama teacher, all siblings actors, early NYC theater, dropped out at 16, 70s TV-film boom, disco culture wave
evidence_summary: Travolta's early career was deeply shaped by his family's immersion in performing arts: his mother was an actress and drama teacher who inspired all six children to become actors. He dropped out of high school at 16 with parental support and moved to New York, landing off-Broadway and Broadway roles as a teenager. His proximity to the New York theater scene and then Hollywood, combined with the 1970s TV and film boom, propelled him to teen idol status at 21 and international stardom at 23 with Saturday Night Fever. The family-domain apprenticeship with his mother was the primary early advantage.

name: Richard Branson
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Virgin Records label in 1973 at age 23 and released Mike Oldfield's Tubular Bells, a major commercial success that established Virgin as a significant music brand.
early_history_summary: Branson launched Student magazine at age 16 in 1966 with Nik Powell, publishing the first issue in January 1968. By 1969 his net worth was estimated at £50,000. He pivoted from the magazine into a mail-order record business in 1970, opened his first record shop on Oxford Street in 1971, and launched the Virgin Records label in 1973, signing Mike Oldfield whose Tubular Bells became a massive hit.
family_context_summary: Born into a middle-class English family in Surrey; father Edward was a barrister and mother Eve was a former ballet dancer and air hostess who supplemented family income with small entrepreneurial ventures. Branson attended the elite Stowe School but left at 16 due to poor academic performance linked to dyslexia.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a barrister following family tradition; mother had entrepreneurial tendencies, making and selling wooden tissue boxes and waste paper bins, and encouraged independence and risk-taking in her children. No direct music or business-industry expertise transferred.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early entrepreneurship, supportive family, London music scene, Stowe School, dyslexia-driven focus, complementary co-founder
evidence_summary: Branson began serious entrepreneurial activity at 16, launching Student magazine and building a mail-order record business by 20. He rode the 1960s-70s music boom in London, a major cultural and commercial wave. His middle-class family provided modest safety and his mother modeled entrepreneurial behavior, but no significant inherited capital or industry networks were documented. His dyslexia and poor academic performance channeled him away from traditional careers and toward business from an early age. Nik Powell served as an early complementary co-founder on Student magazine. By 23, he had founded Virgin Records and released Tubular Bells, a landmark commercial success.

name: Carl Sagan
milestone_by_age_26: Completed PhD thesis at University of Chicago in 1960 at age 25, demonstrating that the greenhouse effect of a thick CO2 and water vapor atmosphere explains Venus's high surface temperature; published multiple papers in PNAS and the Astronomical Journal by age 25-26.
early_history_summary: Sagan entered the University of Chicago at age 16 on a full scholarship in 1951, earning his AB (1954), SB (1955), SM (1956), and PhD (1960) in astronomy and astrophysics under Gerard Kuiper. He was mentored by Enrico Fermi, Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar, Harold Urey, and H.J. Muller, and published his first paper ('Radiation and the Origin of the Gene') in Evolution at age 22 in 1957. His thesis included the Venus greenhouse model and papers on organic matter on the Moon published in PNAS in 1960.
family_context_summary: Born in 1934 in a working-class Jewish neighborhood of Brooklyn, New York. His father Samuel Sagan immigrated from Ukraine and worked as a garment worker; his mother Rachel was described as a major influence. Parents encouraged his scientific curiosity despite modest means.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were not scientists but encouraged intellectual curiosity.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite university, multiple Nobel-caliber mentors, Fermi, Urey, Kuiper, Muller, early university entry at 16, space race, planetary science pioneer
evidence_summary: Sagan entered the University of Chicago at 16 on a full scholarship and was immersed in an extraordinary intellectual environment with mentors including Enrico Fermi, Harold Urey, H.J. Muller, and Gerard Kuiper. By age 25, he had completed his PhD with a significant theoretical model explaining Venus's high surface temperature via the greenhouse effect, and published papers in PNAS and the Astronomical Journal. His working-class background and early university entry at 16 suggest both adversity-driven urgency and exceptional early cognitive ability. The emerging space race provided a structural wave that amplified the significance of his planetary science work.

name: Rupert Murdoch
milestone_by_age_26: Inherited and took over The News, an Adelaide newspaper, at age 22 in 1953 after his father's death, and by age 26 had expanded the business to Perth (Sunday Times, 1956) and multiple other newspapers across Australia.
early_history_summary: Murdoch was born in Melbourne to Sir Keith Murdoch, a prominent newspaper magnate and chairman of Herald and Weekly Times. He was groomed by his father to take over the family business, attending Geelong Grammar and Oxford University. After his father died in 1952, Murdoch returned to Adelaide at age 21 to take charge of News Limited, turning the small Adelaide News into a success and rapidly expanding through acquisitions.
family_context_summary: Son of Sir Keith Murdoch, Australia's most prominent newspaper magnate, and Dame Elisabeth Greene. Raised in a wealthy media family with direct access to the newspaper industry.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a war correspondent turned regional newspaper magnate who owned newspapers in Adelaide, a radio station, and chaired the Herald and Weekly Times publishing company. He actively groomed Rupert for the media business, introducing him to Fleet Street figures.
primary_early_advantage_tags: inherited newspaper, father's media empire, Fleet Street connections, family business succession
evidence_summary: Murdoch inherited News Limited and its Adelaide newspaper at age 22 after his father's death in 1952. His father, Sir Keith Murdoch, was Australia's leading newspaper magnate and had groomed Rupert for the role, introducing him to Fleet Street editors and arranging stints at the Birmingham Gazette and Daily Express. By 26, Murdoch had expanded to Perth and was building a multi-city newspaper group, leveraging inherited distribution, capital, and industry networks.

name: Bernie Madoff
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Bernard L. Madoff Investment Securities LLC in 1960 at age 22, using $5,000 in personal savings and $50,000 borrowed from his in-laws, establishing a legitimate market-making and brokerage firm that grew into the sixth-largest market maker in S&P 500 stocks.
early_history_summary: Madoff grew up in Queens, New York, the son of a plumber-turned-stockbroker. He graduated from Far Rockaway High School in 1956, attended the University of Alabama for one year, then transferred to Hofstra University, earning a bachelor's in political science in 1960. He briefly attended Brooklyn Law School before founding his investment firm with savings from lifeguarding and sprinkler installation work, plus loans from his father-in-law, a successful accountant who referred clients.
family_context_summary: Son of Ralph Madoff, a plumber who later entered the financial industry and co-founded Gibraltar Securities (which was shut down by the SEC), and Sylvia Madoff. Middle-class upbringing in Queens, New York.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father worked as a plumber before entering the financial industry with his wife, founding Gibraltar Securities. This gave Madoff some early exposure to the finance world, though the firm was ultimately forced to close by the SEC.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father-in-law's client referrals, Wall Street proximity, family finance exposure, middle-class outsider drive
evidence_summary: Madoff founded his investment firm at age 22 in 1960, capitalizing on $5,000 in personal savings and $50,000 borrowed from his in-laws. His father-in-law, a successful accountant, referred early clients. His father had transitioned from plumbing to finance, founding Gibraltar Securities, giving Madoff some domain exposure. The firm grew into a major market maker, though Madoff's later infamy stemmed from the Ponzi scheme.

name: Leon Cooper
milestone_by_age_26: Published the seminal paper 'Bound Electron Pairs in a Degenerate Fermi Gas' in Physical Review in November 1956 at age 26, introducing the concept of Cooper pairs that became foundational to the BCS theory of superconductivity and earned the 1972 Nobel Prize in Physics.
early_history_summary: Cooper was born in the Bronx to an immigrant family; his father from Belarus and mother from Poland (who died when he was seven). He attended the Bronx High School of Science, where he won the Westinghouse Science Talent Search, then Columbia University, earning his BA in 1951, MA in 1953, and PhD in 1954 under Robert Serber. After a postdoc at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, he joined John Bardeen at the University of Illinois in 1955 as a research associate, where he developed the Cooper pair concept.
family_context_summary: Son of Irving Kupchik (from Belarus, immigrated after the Russian Revolution) and Anna Zola (from Poland, who died when Leon was seven). His father remarried and changed the family surname to Cooper. Immigrant working-class background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental scientific or academic expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Bronx High School of Science, Columbia University, IAS Princeton, Bardeen collaboration, Westinghouse prize
evidence_summary: Cooper published his seminal Cooper pairs paper at age 26 in November 1956, work that became the foundation of BCS theory and earned the 1972 Nobel Prize. His path ran through Bronx High School of Science (where he won the Westinghouse Science Talent Search), Columbia University (PhD at 24), IAS Princeton, and the University of Illinois where he collaborated with John Bardeen. His immigrant background and early loss of his mother suggest modest family advantages, with his acceleration driven primarily by elite institutional pipelines and an exceptional collaboration with Bardeen and Schrieffer.

name: Warren Buffett
milestone_by_age_26: Founded Buffett Partnership Ltd. in May 1956 at age 25, pooling $105,000 from seven limited partners (all family and personal connections) to launch an investment partnership that eventually grew into Berkshire Hathaway, one of the world's largest conglomerates.
early_history_summary: Buffett was born in Omaha, Nebraska, the son of U.S. Congressman Howard Buffett. He displayed an intense interest in business from childhood, selling gum door-to-door, delivering newspapers, and buying his first stock at age 11. He bought a 40-acre farm at 14 and had $9,800 in savings by college graduation. After attending Wharton and graduating from the University of Nebraska at 19, he earned an MS from Columbia Business School under Ben Graham, then worked at Graham-Newman Corp. from 1954 to 1956 before founding his partnership with $174,000 in personal savings.
family_context_summary: Son of U.S. Congressman Howard Buffett and Leila Stahl Buffett. Grew up in a politically connected, upper-middle-class household in Omaha and Washington, D.C. Father was an investment salesman before entering Congress.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Howard Buffett was a U.S. Congressman and investment salesman who actively cultivated Warren's interest in business and investing, taking him to visit the New York Stock Exchange at age 10 and directing him toward formal education in the field. Father's brokerage office provided Warren's earliest exposure to the stock market.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father's brokerage, Ben Graham mentorship, early investing from age 11, Columbia Business School, congressional family
evidence_summary: Buffett founded his investment partnership at age 25 in 1956, leveraging years of investing experience that began at age 11, mentorship from Ben Graham at Columbia and Graham-Newman, and $174,000 in personal savings. His father, Congressman Howard Buffett, actively cultivated his interest in business and provided access to the brokerage world. The initial partnership capital came entirely from family and personal connections, reflecting strong inherited networks rather than market-proven distribution.

name: Douglas Osheroff
milestone_by_age_26: Co-discovered superfluidity in helium-3 in November 1971 at age 26 as a graduate student at Cornell, making the key experimental observations of phase transitions in helium-3 at ultra-low temperatures. The first paper was published in Physical Review Letters in April 1972, and the discovery earned the 1996 Nobel Prize in Physics.
early_history_summary: Osheroff was born in Aberdeen, Washington, to a working-class family; his father was the son of Jewish immigrants from Russia and his mother was a nurse and daughter of Slovak immigrants. As a teenager he built a 100,000-volt X-ray machine, showing early experimental aptitude. He earned his BS from Caltech in 1967, where he attended lectures by Richard Feynman, then joined Cornell's low-temperature physics laboratory as a graduate student under David Lee, where he made the critical observations leading to the discovery of superfluid helium-3.
family_context_summary: Father was the son of Jewish immigrants from Russia; mother was a nurse and daughter of Slovak immigrants. Working-class background in Aberdeen, Washington, a logging town.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources. No evidence of parental scientific or academic expertise.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Caltech, Cornell low-temperature lab, Lee and Richardson collaboration, Feynman lectures, early experimental aptitude
evidence_summary: Osheroff co-discovered superfluidity in helium-3 at age 26 as a Cornell graduate student, making the critical experimental observations in November 1971 that led to the 1996 Nobel Prize. His path ran through Caltech (BS 1967, Feynman lectures) and Cornell's low-temperature physics lab, where he worked under David Lee with Robert Richardson. His working-class immigrant background offered few inherited advantages; his acceleration came from elite institutional access and an exceptional collaboration with two senior physicists who became his Nobel co-laureates.

name: Claude Shannon
milestone_by_age_26: Published seminal master's thesis 'A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits' in 1938 at age 22, applying Boolean algebra to switching circuit design and founding the field of digital circuit design; won the Alfred Noble Prize for this work in 1940 at age 24.
early_history_summary: Shannon graduated from the University of Michigan with dual degrees in mathematics and electrical engineering at age 20, then went to MIT where he worked on Vannevar Bush's differential analyzer and wrote his groundbreaking master's thesis applying Boolean algebra to relay switching circuits. The thesis, published in 1938, was called 'the most important master's thesis of the century' and won the Alfred Noble Prize in 1940. He completed his PhD in mathematics at MIT in 1940 and joined Bell Labs in 1941.
family_context_summary: Born in Petoskey and raised in Gaylord, Michigan (pop. ~3000), the son of a businessman/probate judge and a high school principal. His father was clever mathematically and gave him radio sets to tinker with; his paternal grandfather was a farmer and inventor with a washing machine patent. A distant relative of Thomas Edison. He built model planes, radio circuits, a radio-controlled boat, and a barbed-wire telegraph to a friend's house as a youth.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a businessman and probate judge who was mathematically inclined and provided radio sets; mother was a language teacher and high school principal; paternal grandfather was an inventor with a patent. No direct family background in engineering or computing, but a culture of tinkering and mathematical interest.
primary_early_advantage_tags: elite institution, MIT, Bell Labs, Vannevar Bush, differential analyzer, Boolean algebra, Alfred Noble Prize
evidence_summary: Shannon graduated from the University of Michigan at 20 with dual degrees in math and EE, then went to MIT where he worked on Vannevar Bush's differential analyzer and wrote a groundbreaking master's thesis (1938, age 22) applying Boolean algebra to switching circuits, founding digital circuit design. He won the Alfred Noble Prize in 1940 for this work, well before age 26. His father was a businessman/probate judge who was mathematically inclined and provided radio sets; his grandfather was an inventor. He benefited from elite institutional pipelines (Michigan, MIT, Bell Labs) and mentorship under Vannevar Bush, but no significant family financial advantage or direct tech-domain inheritance is documented. His scarce intellectual depth in applying mathematical logic to engineering problems was the primary leverage engine.

name: Adam D'Angelo
milestone_by_age_26: Became Chief Technology Officer of Facebook in 2006 at age 22, then co-founded Quora in June 2009 at age 24, both before age 26.
early_history_summary: D'Angelo attended Phillips Exeter Academy where he developed the Synapse Media Player with Mark Zuckerberg. He studied computer science at Caltech (2002-2006) while competing at the highest levels of competitive programming (IOI silver medal 2002, ICPC world finalist). He joined Facebook in 2004 as one of its earliest engineers, became CTO in 2006, and co-founded Quora with Charlie Cheever in June 2009.
family_context_summary: Born in Redding, Connecticut. Attended Phillips Exeter Academy, an elite boarding school, suggesting family resources and emphasis on education. Family financial background is not otherwise documented.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Phillips Exeter, Caltech, competitive programming, IOI silver medal, Zuckerberg, Facebook, ICPC, Silicon Valley
evidence_summary: D'Angelo attended Phillips Exeter Academy where he developed Synapse with Zuckerberg, then studied CS at Caltech while achieving elite competitive programming results (IOI silver medal, ICPC world finalist). He joined Facebook in 2004, became CTO at 22 in 2006, and co-founded Quora at 24 in 2009, all before age 26. His family background is not well documented, but attendance at Phillips Exeter suggests family resources. His primary leverage was scarce technical depth amplified by elite institutional networks (Exeter, Caltech, Facebook) and a high-trust peer relationship with Zuckerberg that opened the Facebook door.

name: Aaron Swartz
milestone_by_age_26: Co-authored the RSS 1.0 specification at age 14 in 2000, became co-owner of Reddit through the Infogami merger in 2005 at age 19, and Reddit was acquired by Conde Nast in 2006 for approximately $5 million at age 20, all well before age 26.
early_history_summary: Swartz was immersed in computing from a young age, creating an encyclopedia website at 12 that won the ArsDigita Prize, and co-authoring the RSS 1.0 specification at 14. He became involved with Creative Commons at 15, enrolled at Stanford in 2004 but left after one year, founded Infogami (which merged with Reddit in 2005), and became a co-owner of Reddit. He also created the web.py framework and helped define Markdown syntax.
family_context_summary: Born in Highland Park, Illinois, to a Jewish family. Father Robert Swartz founded the software firm Mark Williams Company. Attended North Shore Country Day School, a private school near Chicago. Left high school after ninth grade to take courses at Lake Forest College.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father founded and ran the Mark Williams Company, a software firm, providing direct domain exposure to software entrepreneurship from an early age. The family was comfortable enough to send him to private school.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father software company, early internet, RSS 1.0, Reddit, W3C, Creative Commons, ArsDigita Prize, web.py, Markdown
evidence_summary: Swartz was immersed in computing from a very young age, creating an encyclopedia website at 12 (winning the ArsDigita Prize) and co-authoring the RSS 1.0 specification at 14. His father founded the software firm Mark Williams Company, providing direct domain exposure, and he attended a private school in suburban Chicago. He founded Infogami, which merged with Reddit in 2005 at age 19, making him a co-owner; Reddit was acquired by Conde Nast in 2006 for approximately $5 million. He was deeply embedded in early internet communities and the W3C/Creative Commons ecosystem, which provided both technical depth and distribution channels. His primary leverage was early specialization and platform-native compounding through internet communities, catalyzed by his father's software background.

name: Max Rafael Levchin
milestone_by_age_26: Co-founded Fieldlink (later Confinity, then PayPal) with Peter Thiel in 1998 at age 23, serving as CTO and building the anti-fraud systems including one of the first commercial CAPTCHAs; PayPal went public in February 2002 at age 26 and was acquired by eBay later that year.
early_history_summary: Levchin immigrated from Kyiv to Chicago in 1991 at age 16 with his Ukrainian-Jewish family and limited financial resources. He studied computer science at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, founding several small startups including SponsorNet New Media while still a student. In 1998, he co-founded Fieldlink (later Confinity, then PayPal) with Peter Thiel, serving as CTO. He co-created the Gausebeck-Levchin test, one of the first commercial CAPTCHAs. PayPal went public in February 2002 and was acquired by eBay in July 2002.
family_context_summary: Born in Kyiv, Ukrainian SSR, to a Ukrainian-Jewish family. Immigrated to the United States in 1991 at age 16 with limited financial resources, settling in Chicago. Had respiratory problems as a child; doctors doubted his chance of living. Took up the clarinet to expand lung capacity with guidance from his grandmother and parents.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; family was not in the technology domain. Immigrated with just a few hundred dollars.

name: Murray Gell-Mann
milestone_by_age_26: Published the seminal 'Isotopic Spin and New Unstable Particles' paper in Physical Review (November 1953), introducing the concept of strangeness in particle physics.
early_history_summary: Gell-Mann entered Yale at age 15 on a full scholarship and earned his PhD from MIT at 22. By 24, he was at the University of Chicago where he introduced the concept of strangeness, a quantum property explaining decay patterns of certain mesons, published in Physical Review in 1953.
family_context_summary: Born to Austrian Jewish immigrant parents in Manhattan; father worked various jobs including Wall Street and a language school. Mother had ambitions for him. Family was not wealthy but valued education.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father persuaded him to study physics at Yale, correctly predicting he would love quantum mechanics and relativity. Father had intellectual interests but no scientific career.
primary_early_advantage_tags: prodigy, elite schooling, early university entry, physics mentorship
evidence_summary: Gell-Mann was a child prodigy who entered Yale at 15 on scholarship and earned his PhD from MIT at 22. His father, an Austrian immigrant with intellectual interests, guided him toward physics. By 24, he was embedded in the University of Chicago's elite physics community, where he introduced the concept of strangeness—a foundational contribution to particle physics published in Physical Review in 1953.

name: Justin Frankel
milestone_by_age_26: Created and publicly released Winamp, the dominant MP3 player software, at age 19 in 1997; by 1998 it had over 15 million downloads and he founded Nullsoft to distribute it.
early_history_summary: Frankel grew up in Sedona, Arizona, and taught himself programming on his brother's Atari. He ran his school's computer network and wrote an email application for students. After briefly attending the University of Utah in 1996, he dropped out and released the first version of Winamp under his company Nullsoft.
family_context_summary: Son of a lawyer and a postal worker/health food store employee; grew up in a mobile home in Sedona, Arizona. Modest financial background.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-taught programming, early MP3 adoption, internet wave, product taste
